title: Docking split view inside an iframe fails twice: margin:auto shells re-center and halve the freed strip, and doc-space z1 sinks under the host player wrapper so the panel swallows no clicks
trigger: Docked subtitle panel inside an embed iframe renders as a thin strip at the container edge, or renders full-size but is completely unclickable (hit-test returns the player wrapper, resize handle dead)
principle: Strip math assumes the shrunken shell pins to the left edge — a shell with margin:auto (ArtPlayer .art-video-player) re-centers after width shrink, splitting the freed space into left+right gutters and leaving the panel half its expected width; pin margin-left:0 + margin-right:auto on the shell (save/restore like width/height). Separately, doc-space z1 exists to slide under top-level host chrome while scrolling — a child frame has no masthead, so z1 drops the panel below the player's z-10 wrapper and every click is eaten; child frames keep --z-overlay-video. Verify interactivity via elementsFromPoint (top hit must be the panel) plus a real pointer drag, not rects alone.

cases.context: Onflix/playembed iframe: shell .art-video-player 980px container shrunk to 79.6% width but stayed centered (x100 w780) → panel got x880 w100 instead of w200, then z1 put it under the z-10 wrapper → zero interaction.
cases.bad: shell.style.width = pct; /* shell still centered */ ... panel z=1
cases.good: shell: width + marginLeft:'0' + marginRight:'auto' (restored on teardown); docSpace && !childFrame ? z1 : --z-overlay-video

applyFor: docking panels in iframe-hosted players (ArtPlayer, embeds)
any width-shrink + freed-strip layout where the shell self-centers
z-index layering that differs between top-document and child-frame contexts
